overview: A series of systems keeps pushing through the West this week. Heavy Sierra snow and a winter storm hit Wednesday through Friday, then a second system follows late in the weekend, with more active weather into Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong system brings heavy snow and gusty south winds through Friday morning. Winter Storm Warnings cover higher elevations, and thunderstorms are possible in the Valley and foothills Thursday. Kirkwood leads with 72" in total. Friday afternoon brings a brief lull before lighter snow returns Saturday, with active weather continuing into the holiday week.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A winter storm arrives Wednesday and runs through Friday, bringing heavy Sierra snow and strong gusty winds. Mammoth leads the region with 53" in total. The National Weather Service is calling for more, 62 to 86 inches over Wednesday through Sunday night. Lowering snow levels Thursday bring snow into western Nevada valleys and foothill commutes.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Another storm arrives Thursday and runs into Friday, with snow levels falling near or below 5000 feet by Friday. Snowbasin leads the region with 44" in total, and its biggest day is Friday with 25". The system comes in piecemeal, so widespread heavy precipitation looks unlikely. Freezing temperatures near Zion are likely Saturday and Sunday mornings.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A cold front brought the Bighorns snow through this morning, with winter travel on the passes. Another system arrives Thursday through Friday, with precipitation becoming more widespread Friday night. Grand Targhee leads with 26" in total. The Sawtooths and Sun Valley may get a Winter Weather Advisory starting tonight.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Snow ends across the mountains early today, then another round of light snow arrives Thursday night and Friday along the Continental Divide. Gusty winds and a stronger system arrive Saturday, with a cool down through early next week. Wolf Creek leads with 17" in total, and its biggest day is Friday with 7".

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Rain and snow taper early Wednesday, leaving slick mountain passes. Another storm brings measurable snow Friday and Saturday, with the best totals likely in the central mountains of Colorado. Telluride leads with 10" in total. Cold air behind the system keeps afternoon highs below normal.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low moves through Wednesday with mountain snow and lowland rain, then precipitation eases Thursday night. Friday is mostly dry before another system arrives over the weekend. Snow levels near 2500 feet mean snow on the passes. Mt. Bachelor leads with 11" in total, and Crystal Mountain has a possible increase to 3 to 10 inches Wednesday through Monday night.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Flurries are likely Thursday and again through the weekend, with a mix of sun and cloud on Sunday. Fernie leads with 6" in total. A stronger snow chance arrives Monday night, and temperatures stay near or below freezing.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: A mix of sun and cloud gives way to showers and flurries this weekend, with rain by Monday. Cypress Mountain leads with 6" in total, with its biggest day Sunday at 4".

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
